    Robust summary of a heavy-tailed impact metric

    Source: R/metric-summary-robust.R
    sm_metric_summary.Rd

    Summarises a work-level impact metric robustly. Citation-based metrics are heavy-tailed, so the mean is a poor central estimate; this function reports the median with a bootstrap confidence interval and the proportion of papers in the top citation fraction of a chosen reference, alongside the mean. Without an external reference, pp_top10 equals top_pct by construction and does not measure impact relative to other publications.

    Usage

    sm_metric_summary(
  corpus,
  metric = c("citations", "cnci", "rcr", "fwci"),
  robust = TRUE,
  n_boot = 2000L,
  conf = 0.95,
  top_pct = 0.1,
  seed = NULL,
  min_cell = NULL,
  top_reference = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus.

    metric

    Which work-level metric to summarise: "citations" (cited_by_count), "cnci" (field-normalised citation impact, resolved as in sm_its(): a stored impact column such as works$cnci or works$fwci, a corpus$metrics table, else the FNCI that sm_metric_fnci() derives from citation counts), "rcr" (sm_metric_rcr()) or "fwci" (OpenAlex's field-weighted citation impact, works$fwci; see sm_enrich_openalex_impact()).

    robust

    Logical (default TRUE). When TRUE, report the median with a bootstrap CI and pp_top10. When FALSE, report only n, mean, and median (no resampling).

    n_boot

    Number of bootstrap resamples for the median CI (default 2000).

    conf

    Confidence level for the bootstrap interval (default 0.95).

    top_pct

    Single number strictly between 0 and 1: the top fraction of the reference distribution (default 0.1). Ties share credit fractionally. The output column remains named pp_top10 for any fraction.

    seed

    Optional integer seed for reproducible bootstrap resampling. When supplied, the RNG state is saved and restored so the call has no global side effect (mirroring scimapR's reproducibility guarantees).

    min_cell

    For metric = "cnci": NULL (default) or a positive integer, passed to sm_metric_fnci() when the impact is derived from citation counts, as in sm_its().

    top_reference

    Reference for pp_top10: NULL uses the corpus itself; a numeric vector supplies citation counts (at least two after dropping NA); a data frame supplies numeric cited_by_count and optionally year and/or field, matched on keys present in both it and works. Missing keys or unmatched cells are excluded with a message; no matching works gives NA. Reference counts must be finite and non-negative. Data-frame cells may contain a single reference work. "openalex" uses is_top_10pct for top_pct = 0.1 or is_top_1pct for 0.01, averaging non-missing flags; see sm_enrich_openalex_impact().

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    A one-row tibble: metric, n, mean, median, and – when robust = TRUE – median_ci_low, median_ci_high, pp_top10, n_boot. Type-stable: an empty corpus, or for "cnci" a corpus without usable impact data, returns a one-row tibble with n = 0 and NA statistics. The attribute impact_source (character) names where the values come from: for "cnci" the same label as the impact_source of sm_its() (such as "works$fwci (OpenAlex)"), for "fwci" "works$fwci (OpenAlex)", for "citations" "works$cited_by_count" and for "rcr" "sm_metric_rcr()"; it is NA on the n = 0 row. For "cnci" and "fwci" a message (class scimapR_impact_source) names the source too.

    Details

    The bootstrap uses base-R resampling by default; if the optional boot package is installed it is used instead (percentile interval). pp_top10 remains citation-based for every metric; top_reference changes neither the metric summary nor the bootstrap. Tied citation counts share the part of their reference block in the top fraction equally, following Waltman and Schreiber (2013). Using the corpus itself gives top_pct exactly before rounding. An external reference from comparable fields and years, or OpenAlex flags, makes this an informative share.

    For "cnci" and "fwci" only works with a finite value count, and for "cnci" only works of corpus$works (a corpus$metrics table may hold others). metric = "fwci" aborts (class scimapR_no_fwci) when the works have no fwci value.

    References

    Waltman, L., & Schreiber, M. (2013). On the calculation of percentile-based bibliometric indicators. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 64(2), 372–379.

    See also

    sm_summary_works(), sm_count()

    Other counting: sm_citation_maturity(), sm_citation_window(), sm_count()

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_example_corpus(n_works = 100, seed = 1)
sm_metric_summary(corpus, metric = "citations", seed = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   metric        n  mean median median_ci_low median_ci_high pp_top10 n_boot
#>   <chr>     <int> <dbl>  <dbl>         <dbl>          <dbl>    <dbl>  <int>
#> 1 citations   100  15.9     12          10.5             16      0.1   2000

# the real-use fixture carries OpenAlex's FWCI, which "cnci" then uses
fix <- readRDS(sm_example_files("example_realuse_corpus.rds"))
s <- sm_metric_summary(fix, metric = "cnci", robust = FALSE)
#> ℹ Impact source: works$fwci (OpenAlex).
attr(s, "impact_source")
#> [1] "works$fwci (OpenAlex)"
